title: The live bed board
prompt: Nurses want current bed availability, which changes every few minutes, and want to place a hold on a bed from Glean. What do you propose?

options.text: A custom indexed connector that re-crawls the bed board every 15 minutes.
options.feedback: Availability would lag behind reality, and indexing cannot perform the hold. Live retrieval suits data where minutes-to-hours freshness dominates.

options.text: A web history connector so nurses can find bed board pages they visited.
options.feedback: Web history makes page titles from a user's own browsing searchable. It returns no current availability and performs no action.

options.text: A live tool or MCP integration that reads availability and places the hold at request time.
options.feedback: Right. Freshness dominates and a write is required. Tools retrieve current data or perform actions at request time; an index is a snapshot and cannot place a hold.

takeaway: When freshness dominates or the user must act, go live.
